Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. County-level absence established by COMPLETE ENUMERATION, the strongest form of partition argument available. The Kenya Ministry of Health daily situation report relayed by this source names every affected county and its count - 'Twenty-seven (27) counties have reported cases as follows: Garissa (2,859), Mandera (2,281), Nairobi (2,216), Wajir (945), Tana River (780), Kiambu (539), Machakos (491), Kajiado (398), Homa Bay (335), Mombasa (210), Siaya (162), Meru (138), Uasin Gishu (137), Migori (135), Marsabit (115)...' - and the 27 county figures already entered in this file from that list sum to EXACTLY 12 123, the stated national total, leaving no residual to hide an unlisted county in. source: Mutonga et al. 2020, A protracted cholera outbreak among residents in an urban setting, Nairobi county, Kenya, 2015 (Pan African Medical Journal 36:127)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 2014-12-26..2015-06-10. Source states: 'From December 2014 through June 2015, 4,218 cholera cases were reported including 282 (6.7%) confirmed cases and 79 deaths (case fatality rate [CFR] = 1.9%, ranging from zero in Narok county to 5.3% in Mombasa county) from 14 (30%) of Kenya's 47 counties. [Table 1, 14 counties, December 26, 2014-June 10, 2015, Total 4218 (100)]'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. County-level absence by partition from a peer-reviewed complete enumeration. Mutonga et al. 2020 (Kenya FELTP, Pan African Medical Journal 36:127) report that the December 2014 - June 2015 wave affected '14 (30%) of Kenya's 47 counties' and their Table 1 lists all fourteen with counts that sum to EXACTLY the stated national total of 4218 (Migori 915, Nairobi 781, Muranga 619, Homa Bay 469, Kirinyaga 378, Bomet 272, Nakuru 266, Mombasa 189, Embu 179, Machakos 59, Baringo 52, Kilifi 21, Narok 13, Trans Nzoia 5). This county is not among them. The contemporaneous Kenya MoH county situation report of 9 June 2015 (this file's source index 19), one day before the table's cut-off, independently omits it too, so two separate enumerations agree on its absence. CONFLICT DISCLOSED, because it bears on how far this argument can be trusted: those two sources do NOT agree completely. The 9 June 2015 MoH situation report carries Kiambu county at 114 cases and 6 deaths, and Mutonga's fourteen-county table has no Kiambu row at all; the same pair also differ slightly on Machakos (60 vs 59) and Narok (10 vs 13). One county can therefore go missing from the peer-reviewed enumeration, which is why this row is held at confidence 0.75 and why it was written only for counties that BOTH sources exclude. Surveillance system status during absence: OPERATIONAL - this was Kenya's largest epidemic since 2010 and the MoH was publishing county-level cholera situation reports through it; cholera is a priority disease under Kenya's IDSR. REGIONAL CONTEXT: absence during a nationally ACTIVE period, which is the point of the row - it records that Kenya's largest modern epidemic had not, in its first five and a half months, reached this county. PERIOD bounded exactly to the enumeration's own window, 26 December 2014 to 10 June 2015, and not extended: the epidemic went on to reach further counties later in 2015 (Wajir took 750 cases from June 2015, this file Index 74). DOUBLE-COUNTING: provincial subset - do not sum with national row; the national row for this window (this file Index 137, 4218 cases) is primary.

source: WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record 1972-1973, IHR 'Infected Areas' register and weekly cholera notifications (issues 4-52 of 1972 and 1-51 of 1973)
processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1972-07-06..1972-12-31. Source states: 'Infected Areas as on 29 June 1972 - Zones infectees au 29 juin 1972 ... KENYA / Coast Province / Tana River County [WER 1972 no.26]. Infected Areas as on 6 July 1972 - Zones infectees au 6 juillet 1972 [WER 1972 no.27: no Kenyan area listed, and none in any subsequent issue of 1972 or 1973].'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. This rests on a POSITIVE REGISTER, which is why it is labelled Documented rather than Inferred. Under the International Health Regulations (1969) the WER printed in every weekly issue a complete worldwide list of the administrative areas formally declared infected with cholera, and an area was struck off only after an affirmative removal once it had been free of infection for the prescribed period. Being off that register is an official statement that no area of the country is infected - quite unlike being missing from a case table, which is what I refused to treat as absence for 2003, 2019 and 2026. Kenya's trail through 1972 is continuous and then stops: issue 4 notifies one case and no deaths in Wajir County for 9-15 January, issue 8 lists Marsabit County, issue 12 Coast Province, and issue 26 ('Infected Areas as on 29 June 1972') lists Tana River County, Coast Province. From issue 27 ('Infected Areas as on 6 July 1972') Kenya is absent, and stays absent through issues 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48 and 50 of 1972 - fifteen registers checked one by one - and through 1973. The only later Kenya mentions in any of those issues are imported-malaria country-of-origin lists (1972 no.38, 1973 no.34) and a notice of the WHO Inter-regional Seminar on Epidemiological Surveillance of Communicable Diseases held in Nairobi in October 1972 (1972 no.50); each was opened and read rather than counted. TL set to 6 July 1972, the date of the first register from which Kenya is absent, which is conservative: IHR removal implies the last case preceded it by at least the prescribed free period, so the true absence began earlier. Surveillance system status during absence: OPERATIONAL - Kenya was filing dated weekly cholera notifications to WHO in the same year (the Wajir County entry for 9-15 January), notified an annual total of 51 cases for 1972, and hosted WHO's Inter-regional Seminar on Epidemiological Surveillance in Nairobi in October 1972. CONTINUITY: this row runs straight into the existing 1973 national absence row (this file Index 171), whose source is WHO's own statement that cholera 'reappeared in three countries (Chad, Kenya, and Togo) that had remained free of infection in 1973', giving a continuous documented Kenyan cholera-free period of roughly eighteen months from July 1972 to the end of 1973. REGIONAL CONTEXT: absence during a regionally ACTIVE period - the seventh pandemic was at its African peak, and the same registers list infected areas in Cameroon, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Malawi, Nigeria and Zaire in the same weeks. DOUBLE-COUNTING: this row sits inside the JHU national annual row for 1972 (51 cases); the JHU annual row is primary for the 1972 total and this row is primary for within-year timing - do not sum with national row.

source: IRIN, Kenya: Water shortages lead to cholera outbreaks (Nairobi, 10 September 2009)
processing_notes: Source states: 'In the capital Nairobi, three cholera cases were reported in the eastern Dandora area seven days ago. source: IFRC Weekly News 09/99, Kenya: Cholera alert (5 March 1999)
